name: OSWorld 2.0
rationale: Best current long-horizon desktop signal; has an independent audit caveat to surface.

name: Terminal-Bench 2.1
rationale: Widely submitted execution benchmark with a public provenance contract.

name: WebArena-Verified
rationale: Verified replacement for original WebArena.

name: TheAgentCompany
rationale: Enterprise software-company environment with versioned per-run artefacts.

name: τ³-bench
rationale: Current generation of the τ tool+policy lineage.

name: τ²-bench
rationale: Historical protocol retained for continuity; not comparable with τ³.

name: AppWorld
rationale: Clean machine-readable leaderboard JSON.

name: OSWorld-Verified
rationale: Verified revision of original OSWorld; kept separate from 2.0.

name: MCPMark Verified
rationale: Reproducible real MCP workflows with automated verifiers.

name: MCP-Atlas
rationale: Broad MCP tool coverage; LLM-judge scoring needs judge identity pinned.

name: VisualWebArena
rationale: Vision-first web-control signal; keep separate from WebArena-Verified.

name: GAIA
rationale: Public result dataset makes it cleanly ingestible; largely superseded visually by newer research benchmarks.

name: SWE-bench Verified
rationale: Coding-agent baseline; secondary because this page spans more than coding.

name: AndroidWorld
rationale: Mobile GUI grounding; environment revision matters.

name: Windows Agent Arena
rationale: Windows-side desktop signal; difficulty mode is a protocol field.

name: Online-Mind2Web
rationale: Live-web successor to original Mind2Web; auto-eval vs human-eval differ.

name: BFCL V4
rationale: Agentic function/tool calling incl. web search and memory domains.

name: OSWorld-MCP
rationale: Directly compares GUI vs MCP tool invocation in computer-use agents.

name: SkillsBench
rationale: Measures skill use under different harness/model combinations.

name: DeepSWE v1.1
rationale: Long-horizon SWE with explicit harness/model identity.

name: SWE-bench Pro
rationale: Public/private task sets must not be mixed.

name: TUA-Bench
rationale: Terminal-use signal beside Terminal-Bench; leaderboard is README-only.

name: OfficeQA Pro
rationale: Enterprise grounded reasoning over a document corpus; corpus representation is a protocol field.

name: ToolSandbox
rationale: Stateful conversational tool use; secondary until current-model coverage improves.

name: AgentBench FC
rationale: Historic multi-environment signal; must be pinned to the FC revision.

name: WebLINX 1.1
rationale: BrowserGym-compatible revision; store as WebLINX-1.1.

name: Mind2Web (original)
rationale: Static offline tasks; largely replaced by Online-Mind2Web and WebArena-Verified.

name: MiniWoB++
rationale: Toy-scale; retained only as a historical sanity check.

name: WebVoyager
rationale: Live-web navigation; GPT-judge scoring and drift make it a weak canonical source.

name: PaperBench
rationale: Replication-of-research-agent benchmark; expensive and narrow.

name: ProgramBench
rationale: Secondary coding signal; preserve solved vs >=95% tests metrics.

name: PostTrainBench
rationale: Specialist post-training agent benchmark; pin v1/v1.1 and seed count.

name: Long Horizon Terminal Benchmark
rationale: Complement to Terminal-Bench; some runs use non-standard time budgets.

name: AgentIF
rationale: Instruction/constraint following diagnostic, not an execution benchmark.

name: CoWorkBench (vendor-internal)
rationale: Vendor-internal benchmark with no public tasks/protocol; cannot be a canonical comparable source.

name: JobBench (vendor-internal)
rationale: Vendor-internal; may be stored as vendor-reported evidence but not a public benchmark.

name: Vision2Web (vendor-internal)
rationale: Vendor-internal; no public tasks or evaluation protocol.

name: TimeWarp
rationale: Emerging desktop benchmark; monitor for current-model coverage.

name: OpenApps
rationale: Open-ended desktop apps; coverage thin for tracked families.
